labels.description: The customer-facing technology risk now covers adopting AI tools and other technology innovations, adds inaccuracies and launches of new or emerging technologies as causes of disruption, and adds damage to brand and reputation as a consequence in both the heading and the body.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new exposures (AI tool adoption, new technology launches, inaccuracies) are disclosed, and criterion 3: severity widens to include brand and reputation damage.

labels.description: Political instability and geopolitical tensions are added as sources of supply chain disruption, the COVID-19 pandemic framing of the strain and online demand passages is dropped, and 'increased supply chain costs' is broadened to 'increased costs'.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new disruption sources (political instability, geopolitical tensions) are disclosed, and criterion 2: the COVID-19 pandemic references in the second paragraph are dropped.

labels.description: The safety risk now names negative publicity about the Company and incidents such as civil unrest, raids and protests at stores and facilities, and adds store traffic and associate recruiting to the adverse impacts, while heightened shrink moves to past tense ('have seen' to 'saw').
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new exposures (Company publicity, civil unrest, raids, protests) and new impacts (store traffic, recruiting) are disclosed, and criterion 3: the shrink characterization shifts from ongoing to past.

labels.description: The cybersecurity and privacy risk adds a statement that risk management processes may not be implemented or effective, AI-enabled threat actors and novel attacks, South America to the listed geopolitical conflicts, AI and emerging technology regulation, international privacy laws, and a new sentence on substantial compliance costs including reporting and disclosure regimes.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: new risks (ineffective risk management processes, AI-enabled attacks, compliance cost) are disclosed, and criterion 2: a new jurisdiction (South America) and new regulation areas (AI, international privacy laws) are referenced.

labels.description: The labor risk replaces 'public health concerns' with 'safety and security in our stores and other facilities' as a labor factor, drops SRS as the location of union-represented associates, softens union organizing from 'we are also subject to' to 'we may be subject to future' efforts, drops the supply chain investments reference, and adds associates with specialized knowledge to serve Pros.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a labor factor is swapped (public health removed, store safety added), criterion 2: the SRS business reference is dropped, and criterion 3: union organizing is softened from realized to hypothetical.

labels.description: A new sentence discloses that offering new payment options may subject the Company to additional rules, regulations and compliance requirements and higher fraud losses, alongside a rename of the 'Pro House Account trade credit' program to 'Pro Trade Credit' and 'artificial intelligence' shortened to 'AI'.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new exposure (added regulation and higher fraud losses tied to new payment options) is disclosed, which outweighs the program rename and stylistic edits.
